canonical_name: De Giorgi-Nash interior Holder regularity theorem
source_metadata_claim: Weak solutions of divergence-form equations are Holder continuous.
canonical_statement: Candidate family: a weak solution of a scalar, second-order, uniformly elliptic divergence-form homogeneous equation with bounded measurable coefficients on a Euclidean domain has a locally Holder-continuous representative, with quantitative interior control depending on dimension and ellipticity data.
domain_and_universes: Candidate only: finite-dimensional Euclidean domain, real scalar-valued Sobolev weak solution; exact dimension and Lean universes remain unfrozen.
quantifiers: dimension n and domain Omega (exact restrictions open)
measurable coefficient field A with boundedness and uniform ellipticity constants
Holder exponent alpha and quantitative constant (dependency and quantifier order open)
hypotheses: scalar divergence-form homogeneous elliptic equation in the weak sense
local Sobolev membership and an interior containment condition
conclusion: A locally Holder-continuous representative of u, with the exact oscillation/seminorm estimate still to be frozen from a pinpointed source theorem.
excluded_scope: replacement by local boundedness or a Harnack inequality alone
degenerate_cases: Zero solution is allowed but trivial; empty/interiorless domains and balls not compactly contained in the domain must not make the eventual theorem vacuous. Dimension, ellipticity-constant, and radius boundary cases require statement-phase mutation tests.

alternate_encodings.target: oscillation decay on concentric interior balls
